page: Microsoft Azure FX96-24ms_v2 is a memory-intensive server instance powered by the Intel Xeon 8573C processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, it features 24 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor runs at a high clock speed of 4.2 GHz and is equipped with a substantial 260 MB L3 cache. It is configured with an exceptionally large memory capacity of 1832.0 GB, yielding 76.33 GB of RAM per core. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with Geekbench single-core and text processing scores placing in the top tier (top 10%). Multi-core performance and image processing are also strong, ranking in the top 25%. Memory write bandwidth for large uncached blocks is measured at 118.92 GB/sec, which is in the top 25%, while read bandwidth remains in the average range. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks show strong performance, as does text generation for small language models.

Given its massive memory-to-vCPU ratio, the FX96-24ms_v2 offers high resource density for memory-bound applications, allowing organizations to run large-scale in-memory databases and complex analytical workloads without paying for excess CPU cores. The combination of a high 4.2 GHz clock speed and massive RAM makes it highly suitable for enterprise database hosting, large-scale caching layers, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.
